case_name: Chain Singh Kapoor vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Ors
facts_of_case: Informant's daughter called her at 3:10 p.m. and told her that her father (the present petitioner) had visited the home with a security person and a female, removed her articles from one room and kept them in another room. The police registered the F.I.R. and conducted the investigation.

legal_principles.principle: A complaint can be quashed where the allegations made in the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out the case alleged against the accused.
legal_principles.held: The principles relating to the exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash complaints and criminal proceedings have been stated and reiterated by this Court in several decisions.
cited_cases: Madhavrao Jiwajirao Scindia v. Sambhajirao Chandrojirao Angre, [(1988) 1 SCC 692: 1988 SCC (Cri) 234]

legal_principles.principle: A complaint may also be quashed where it is a clear abuse of the process of the court, as when the criminal proceeding is instituted with an ulterior motive or in spite of the fact that the allegations made in the complaint do not constitute any offence.
